about: Expected result-block values for the Tonewick rehearsal ROM and the release ROM's auto QA run, judged by tools/judge.py. Block layout: arm9/source/game/lab.h. Every item reads one or two raw measurements (values[1..36]) taken by the ROM with the capture units and the system devices, and the range or value GBATEK gives; a value a capture never reached is 0xFFFF, which fails every range, eq and mask item here (the RTC item names it in not_value). Items carry "done": the completion bit of their district in values[0] (the audit ran; it does not say its captures finished). The RTC item is n/a when the run was before noon. "frame" is the minimum number of frames to run, per boot. "known" lists, per emulator version and renderer, the gating items expected to fail there; judge.py --profile passes only when the failing set matches exactly. The save items need a save chip (env "cart", n/a when the run has none).

rehearsal.note: every district's lines solved by script and audited in order; no save chip, no NitroFS

qa.note: the release ROM's hidden auto QA mode (title: hold L+R+X+Y for 120 frames): all four districts played by key script, the credits; the block uses the rehearsal's layout and adds the QA words at values[48..54] (verdict 1 PASS / 2 FAIL, log lines, SD flags, last state hash, checkpoints, lag, save flags)

sources.report:<ref>: a hardware report by a third party; gating
sources.hw:<model>: measured by us on real hardware; gating
sources.rom: decided by the ROM's own deterministic logic, independent of the emulator; gating
sources.unconfirmed: no hardware value yet; informational only, never fails the run

items.title: The mixer capture works: a full-scale 2 kHz square wave (PSG duty 3, volume 127, divider 0) captures with a peak-to-peak swing of 1000 to 65534
PSG duty 3 captures as a clean square wave: 120 to 136 sign changes in 1024 samples (64 cycles at 2 kHz)
PSG duty 7 is 0.0 % HIGH: the output stays LOW (about -7FFFh), not silent (the captured mean is below -16384; 12.5 % HIGH would read about -24575 + 32768 = 8193, so 0 to 4095 only)
Volume divider 3 divides by 16, not by 8 (the swing ratio of divider 0 to divider 3 is 16.0, x10 = 150 to 170)
Volume register 127 counts as 128 (N = 0..126, 128): the level at 127 is exactly twice the level at 64 (ratio x1000 = 1995 to 2005)
A one-shot channel with PNT+LEN of 3 words (below the 4-word minimum) keeps the busy bit set after the sound should have ended (a 4-word one-shot clears it)
... and, looped, makes no sound (the captured peak is at most 2)
Without the hold bit a one-shot sound ends in silence (the captured level is at most 5 % of the looped level)
With the hold bit a one-shot sound keeps its last sample after it ended (90 to 110 % of the looped level)
items.level_basis: gbatek:DS Sound Channels; gbatek:DS Sound Notes

items.title: The noise channel follows the GBATEK shift register (X = X SHR 1, carry: LOW and XOR 6000h, else HIGH; accepted from any offset of the 32767-step sequence): at least 240 captured bits match the model

An ADPCM loop started in the data part (word 9, not the header) repeats exactly: index and PCM16 value are reloaded to the values that appeared at the loop start (the drift between two passes is at most 3 %)
A PCM8 capture of a 3412h level stores the upper byte, 34h
A capture length of 0 is read as 1 word: exactly one word of a sentinel buffer changes
Capture 0 with source bit 1 (and add off) records channel 0 alone: with channel 0 and channel 1 both playing 2000h it captures 2000h, not the mixer sum 4000h (+32768 = 40960 +-0.4 %)
Capture 0 with source bit 1 and add on is not clipped but ANDed with FFFFh: 7000h + 7000h reads -2000h (+32768 = 24576)
Capture 0 with source bit 1 and add off records -8000h when channel 0 and channel 1 are both negative (+32768 = 0)
In 24 hour mode the RTC hour register carries the AM/PM flag (read only, set for hours 12 to 23): every one of 8 raw reads is consistent. n/a before noon, when the flag is 0 either way
Power management registers 4 to 7Fh mirror 0..3 on the original DS, and 5, 6, 7 mirror 4 and 8..7Fh mirror 0..7 on the DS Lite (rule by firmware byte 1Dh; n/a for any other model)
The EEPROM write latch is set after WREN
... and reset after the WRITE ran
Status register bits 4 to 6 of an 8 KB to 64 KB EEPROM are always 0
At least one of the two firmware user-settings copies has a good CRC16 (over 70h bytes)
The newest copy (the one whose update counter is one above the other, modulo 80h) is the copy the loader left at 027FFC80h (saved by the ARM7 before its own start-up replaces it)
All twelve signal lines were cleared (the rehearsal script, or the QA pilot at the levers)
All four districts ran their audit to the end
The rehearsal (or the QA run) reached its end and published its block
The QA run ended with PASS (QARN verdict 1)
